key_insight: Fixed schema graphs are not necessary: learning full-resolution (tuple-level) graph structure end-to-end yields more accurate and robust relational representations than relying on a single fixed schema-derived graph.
problem_solved: Relational Deep Learning often depends on a fixed graph built from database schema (the full-resolution principle), which can be suboptimal, brittle to schema design, and unable to capture latent tuple-level relations needed for accurate relational prediction.
method: Perform graph-structure learning at full resolution (tuple/node level) by scoring and learning edges during GNN training rather than using a fixed schema graph.
Introduce schema-aware inductive biases and regularizers (e.g., sparsity, block priors) to preserve relational semantics while allowing discovery of missing/latent links.
Integrate the learned structure end-to-end with relational GNNs using efficient parameterizations and sampling to keep training scalable on real RDBs.
impact: Reduces manual graph engineering and sensitivity to schema choices, improving accuracy and robustness on relational prediction tasks; practical for ML teams working directly on relational databases who want end-to-end, data-driven graph construction.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: fixed schema graph (static edges) vs learned full-resolution graph (dynamic, weighted edges between tuples).
Pipeline flowchart: RDB -> tuple nodes -> edge scoring module -> learned graph -> relational GNN -> predictions.
Bar/line chart: performance comparison (accuracy/AUC) of fixed-schema baselines vs full-resolution graph-structure learning across tasks/datasets.
Schematic illustrating constraints: icons for sparsity, schema priors, and scalability (e.g., sampled mini-batches) to show practical training considerations.
paper_title: Is Fixing Schema Graphs Necessary? Full-Resolution Graph Structure Learning for Relational Deep Learning
paper_authors: Yi Huang, Qingyun Sun, Jia Li, Xingcheng Fu, Jianxin Li
